page_title: Identify an animal by photo or video: how apps do it and what works best

sources.entry: Nature GO - Android app that suggests the species of a bird, insect, mammal or plant from an 8-second video filmed in the app, shows the visible evidence, and can also name a gallery photo. #freemium

summary.name: Nature GO
summary.one_liner: Nature GO is an Android and iPhone app that suggests the species of a bird, insect, mammal, plant or other creature from an 8-second live video filmed in the app.
use_cases: identify a bird seen in the garden
log insects and wildlife on a walk
check a species suggestion before recording it
learn common US animals and their frequency
summary.what_it_does: The app suggests a species from an 8-second live video filmed in the app, where the user moves the phone left or right as asked; the server checks four frames and the movement. It can also suggest a name from a gallery photo, but only live video adds a species to the catalogue. The catalogue has 151 widespread species in five drawers (Birds, Plants, Insects, Mammals, Others), and other finds go to Beyond the 151. An AI field mentor, Professor Hazel, adds a field note and a next species to look for, labelled as AI. The page also gives GBIF data on the most observed US animals for September 17 to October 16, 2026.
notable: Species added only from an 8-second live video, not a gallery photo
Professor Hazel AI field mentor with field notes
No account needed; notes and place labels stay on the phone
caveats: Requires an internet connection because identification runs on a server
Free tier limited to 3 analyses a day; Nature GO Plus raises this to 10 a day while capacity lasts
Never states whether a plant, fungus or animal is edible, venomous or safe
